artists.name: Buddy Guy
artists.comment: An electric-blues giant whose sting, swing, and fearless stage energy still make the form feel alive and dangerous.

artists.name: B.B. King
artists.comment: A placeholder for regal phrasing, warm vibrato, and solos that say more by doing less.

artists.name: Muddy Waters
artists.comment: Keep this slot for Chicago blues foundations that still sound elemental rather than historical.

artists.name: Howlin' Wolf
artists.comment: A place for the rougher edge of the tradition: huge presence, stark lines, and unforgettable force.

artists.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan
artists.comment: Useful for guitar playing that turns control, speed, and feeling into one continuous motion.

artists.name: Pink Floyd
artists.comment: A band that made atmosphere structural: patient builds, huge spaces, and albums that feel like complete worlds.

artists.name: Radiohead
artists.comment: A placeholder note for albums that still feel strange, precise, and alive.

artists.name: The Beatles
artists.comment: Useful as a reminder that melodic clarity and experiment do not cancel each other out.

artists.name: Led Zeppelin
artists.comment: Reserve this slot for music with weight, motion, and a sense of physical space.

artists.name: The Smashing Pumpkins
artists.comment: Good for louder records that still carry fragility inside the distortion.

artists.name: Mahmood
artists.comment: Italian pop that balances immaculate hooks with bruised intimacy; sleek on the surface, but emotionally restless underneath.

artists.name: Frank Ocean
artists.comment: A placeholder for pop writing that stays fluid, evasive, and emotionally exact.

artists.name: FKA twigs
artists.comment: Keep this for music where body, texture, and design feel inseparable from the song itself.

artists.name: Rosalia
artists.comment: A good slot for artists who can make tradition and futurism sound natural in the same breath.

artists.name: Caroline Polachek
artists.comment: Useful for polished pop that still takes melodic and emotional risks.

artists.name: Aphex Twin
artists.comment: A placeholder for electronic detail that keeps revealing new structure over time.

artists.name: Boards of Canada
artists.comment: For music that feels half-memory, half-signal, and impossible to flatten into one mood.

artists.name: Four Tet
artists.comment: A future note can live here about patience, rhythm, and quiet surprise.

artists.name: Burial
artists.comment: A useful slot for city-night records that sound distant and intimate at once.

artists.name: Daft Punk
artists.comment: Keep this one for electronic music that pairs strong design with real emotional lift.

artists.name: Miles Davis
artists.comment: A placeholder for records that reduce everything to tone, timing, and restraint.

artists.name: John Coltrane
artists.comment: This slot works well for intensity that still feels searching rather than closed.

artists.name: Bill Evans
artists.comment: A home for piano recordings that create focus without becoming background music.

artists.name: Charles Mingus
artists.comment: For larger, more unruly ensembles that somehow land exactly where they should.

artists.name: Chet Baker
artists.comment: Useful for the quieter edges of the collection where vulnerability leads the sound.

artists.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
artists.comment: A placeholder for architecture, repetition, and the feeling that order can still sing.

artists.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
artists.comment: Keep this for works that start as argument and end as something larger than force.

artists.name: Claude Debussy
artists.comment: A good home for color, ambiguity, and pieces that move like changing light.

artists.name: Franz Schubert
artists.comment: Use this for music that sounds simple at first and devastating once it settles in.

artists.name: Maurice Ravel
artists.comment: Another placeholder for craft so exact that it starts to feel almost unreal.

artists.name: Kendrick Lamar
artists.comment: A place for albums where technical control and moral pressure move together.

artists.name: A Tribe Called Quest
artists.comment: Good for records that stay playful, warm, and rhythmically sharp at the same time.

artists.name: Nas
artists.comment: Use this slot for writing that turns scene, history, and voice into one gesture.

artists.name: J Dilla
artists.comment: A placeholder for the producers whose timing changes how everything else feels.

artists.name: Nujabes
artists.comment: Reserve this one for music that stays gentle without becoming slight.

artists.name: Bon Iver
artists.comment: A place for records that sound like weather, memory, and interior monologue.

artists.name: Sufjan Stevens
artists.comment: Useful for the part of the catalog where detail and tenderness keep changing scale.

artists.name: Phoebe Bridgers
artists.comment: Keep this slot for songs that stay understated while still cutting very deep.

artists.name: Nick Drake
artists.comment: A placeholder note for spare arrangements that leave a long afterimage.

artists.name: Fleet Foxes
artists.comment: Good for harmonies and songs that make open space feel almost architectural.
